rubrics.criterion: No callable in the serf package's reply pipeline accepts a cluster peer's network address, UDP port and node name as separate sibling parameters. This covers at least the callables involved in assembling an outgoing query, acknowledging a received query, delivering a reply directly over UDP, sending a query response (and its ack) toward the originator, duplicating a response through relay members, the per-member relay hop send, forwarding a relayed envelope from the decoded relay header, constructing the client-facing query event, and re-dialing a failed member -- whether the solver re-bundled the destination into one value, restructured the call chain, or removed a seam entirely.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core outcome of the task: the peer reply-destination data clump in the reply pipeline is gone at every internal parameter list that previously repeated it. It is gradable directly from the solver's patch and repository state, and any sound re-bundling (reusing existing bundled types or a new dedicated one) satisfies it.

rubrics.criterion: At the pipeline's sources of the destination data -- incoming query messages, the local member record at query issuance, the decoded relay envelope, live member records chosen for relay hops, and tracked failed-member state -- the destination now crosses into the pipeline as one bundled value read from its existing owner, without intermediate members-first re-packing that exists only to hand the pieces onward.
rubrics.rationale: The clump's cost is paid at the boundaries where bundled owners leak their members into loose locals. Repairing only the deepest signatures while re-decomposing at the sources would leave the traveling group alive in a thinner form, so the source-side hand-offs are an independent, gradable part of resolution for this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The overlap accumulated on the shared send path is not carried forward: the callable that sends a query response no longer receives the message's Lamport timestamp and identifier as standalone parameters alongside the response structure that already carries those same fields (they are read from the given response data instead, or otherwise folded into the bundled design).
rubrics.rationale: This instance deliberately contains a merge artifact on the shared ack/response send seam where two formerly separate call chains met. The prompt calls this redundancy out explicitly as 'not carried forward', so resolving it is an instance-specific obligation independent of the re-bundling itself.

rubrics.criterion: Every call site of the re-bundled callables constructs the bundled destination from the source actually in scope at that site (query message fields, local member state, relay header fields, member records in the relay loop, failed-member state, or client-event state) so that each stage passes one coherent value to the next without re-exposing the three members between stages.
rubrics.rationale: Re-bundling one signature means nothing without adapting the callers that feed it. For this case the callers are spread across the query, response, relay-forward and rejoin stages and pull the destination from six distinct owner shapes, so the call-side adaptation is a separate observable outcome from the signature-side design.

rubrics.criterion: The client-facing query event keeps exactly its current observable surface: its exported accessors and string behavior are unchanged, it still exposes the query's source node and deadline and nothing more of the originator's endpoint, and a client answering through the event still produces answers addressed to the same peer as before the change.
rubrics.rationale: The pipeline stores reply-destination state on the event value a client later answers through; a solver could be tempted to change what the event exposes or to drop private destination state from it. This keeps the client-facing contract fixed while allowing the private representation to change.

rubrics.criterion: The representation drift that previously forced hop-by-hop conversions is reconciled coherently: within the transformed pipeline the bundled destination carries one address representation and one port width, and the only width/representation conversions remaining are at struct-field boundaries that legitimately require another type (wire fields, member fields), not between internal callables.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's clump carried two address representations and two port widths across its hops, each with site-local conversions. Undoing that drift coherently -- rather than wrapping a bundled value that still needs a conversion at every hop -- is an observable design property of any sound repair for this case.

rubrics.criterion: No shim remains whose only purpose is to bridge old and new forms: no wrapper that unpacks a bundled destination into the old address/port/name members to call an unmodified implementation, and no wrapper that re-packs members into the bundled value only to forward to the new form.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible near-miss repair in this pipeline keeps every existing body untouched and adds pack/unpack adapters at each boundary, which satisfies no signature list but retains the clump as a live pattern. The prompt's definition of done explicitly excludes such forwarding scaffolding.

rubrics.criterion: The artifacts of the scattered form were actually removed where the pipeline was re-bundled: the memberwise address/port/name locals in the relay-ingest dispatch and in the failed-member rejoin sweep (which existed solely to pass the pieces into the next call) do not survive alongside the bundled form, and no unmodified memberwise variant of a re-bundled callable remains reachable from the pipeline.
rubrics.rationale: The change the solver receives introduced these locals as pure pass-through staging, and leaving them (or a parallel memberwise copy of a helper) in place keeps dead scaffolding in the exact stages the task names, which a verifier can observe directly in the patch.

rubrics.criterion: No message that reaches the network changes shape: query messages, delivery acknowledgments, query responses and relay envelopes still encode exactly the fields, types and ordering they had before, so a node running the change interoperates with a released-version node in a mixed cluster (including join/snapshot exchanges).
rubrics.rationale: The re-bundled destination sits directly on the encode/decode path for query, ack, response and relay traffic, so this is the highest-risk regression surface of a plausible repair in this instance, and it is observable from the patch's treatment of the wire structures.

rubrics.criterion: Existing log output is preserved verbatim in the touched stages: the format strings and emission conditions for the query-acknowledgment path (format failure, send failure, relay failure), the relay-forward failure in the memberlist delegate, and the reconnect attempts in the failed-member rejoin path are byte-identical, logging the same address and node representations as before.
rubrics.rationale: Several stages in this pipeline log destination-derived strings that operators and the test-suite assertions rely on. A repair that re-bundles destinations can silently change which form of the address gets logged (for example switching between an address-only and name-prefixed form), which is an instance-specific regression this case must guard.

rubrics.criterion: Reply and rejoin behavior stays semantically identical: a failed direct delivery of an acknowledgment still relays the duplicate copy; response size limits, one-response-per-query enforcement and past-deadline rejection behave as before; relay duplication still requires a positive relay factor and enough other members; and the rejoin target string keeps its node-name-prefixed form whenever a node name is present.
rubrics.rationale: These are the behavioral invariants recorded for this case's ack, response, relay and rejoin stages; each is individually observable in the solver's patch because the repair touches exactly the callables that enforce them.

rubrics.criterion: Locking and read-safety around member-derived destinations is preserved: the failed-member fields used to build a rejoin target are still read while the member lock is held and the lock is still released before dialing, and the relay-hop selection still operates on member state consistent with the existing concurrency model of the pipeline.
rubrics.rationale: The failed-member rejoin stage in this case reads shared member state under a lock specifically so the dial can happen outside it; re-bundling touches that exact read, and a repair that moves member-field reads outside the lock scope would create a data race the full test command may only expose intermittently, so it is graded explicitly.
